title: Let the DSP48 post-adder make the first adder-tree level (pair sums of packed products)
hypothesis:
# Let the DSP48 post-adder make the first adder-tree level (pair sums of packed products)

Category: area

## Motivation
With D=128 and MCOLS=2 the integer dot product dominates the fabric: `g_tree` reduces 128 products
per column to one value in LUTs. That is 127 operand reductions per column, 254 in total, each a
carry-save row or carry chain about 17 to 24 bits wide. The first level `s2` also needs
2 x 32 x 20 = 1280 fabric flops. Column 0 has an extra cost: each of its 128 products carries a
`pp[15]` borrow bit into the tree, so every even-column `s2` group is really an 8-operand add.
This level is most of the 13009 LUTs and about a quarter of the 5384 FFs. Meanwhile the 128
DSP48E1s that make the packed products (MREG only, after r20260924-030158-s0) leave their
post-adder and P register unused.

## Change (rtl/mxu/otpu_mxu.sv, `g_tree` only)
Pair up the positions i = 2q and 2q+1 of each packed column pair p. The ALU of DSP (p,2q+1) adds
the two packed products, and its P register replaces the first fabric level:

```
localparam logic [33:0] PK = 34'd32513;   // low-field offset, odd (see below)
logic [MCOLS/2-1:0][D-1:0][33:0]   pm;    // packed products   (DSP M registers)   S1
logic [MCOLS/2-1:0][D/2-1:0][33:0] pq;    // packed pair sums  (DSP P registers)   S2
pm[p][i]  <= 34'(pa * w0[i]);                            // pa = a_{2p}*2^16 + a_{2p+1}, as today
pq[p][q]  <= pm[p][2q+1] + (pm[p][2q] + PK);             // DSP 2q: M + C(=PK), PREG=0 ->
                                                         // DSP 2q+1: M + C, PREG=1
```
Both adds are the standard M + C post-adder pattern that `xilinx_dsp` packs. DSP 2q has
C = constant PK and PREG=0. DSP 2q+1 has C = DSP 2q's P, either through fabric or turned into
PCIN by `xilinx_dsp_cascade`, plus PREG=1. The DSP-to-DSP path is MREG to P comb (1671 ps in the
yosys model) plus C setup (1244 ps), about 2.9 ns, far below the 4.7 ns critical path.

Field extraction is exact, with no borrow logic. Let E be the even column's pair sum and O the odd
column's pair sum. Each lies in [-32512, 32768] (two int8 x int8 products). Then
pq = E*2^16 + (O + PK). With PK = 32513, O + PK lies in [1, 65281], which fits an unsigned 16-bit
field. So:
- even column 2p: `$signed(pq[32:16])` (17 bit) is exactly E;
- odd column 2p+1: `{1'b0, pq[15:0]}` is exactly O + PK. The column total subtracts (D/2)*PK
  once, as the initial value of that column's `s4` sum (a 32-bit constant).

PK is odd so `opt_expr` cannot trim trailing constant-zero bits from the `+PK` adder, which would
break the post-adder match.

Downstream, S3 becomes `s3[j][g]` = the sum of 8 pair values, 20-bit signed (D/16 groups: at most
8*65281 < 2^19 unsigned, or 8*|E| <= 2^18 signed). S4 is `s4[j]` = (odd j ? -(D/2)*PK : 0) +
the sum of the D/16 `s3` values, exactly as today's s4. There are still four register levels
(M, P, s3, s4), so `LDOT`, `m1..m4` and `ws1..ws4` don't change. Latency and throughput are
identical.

An odd last column (MCOLS odd, not in the board build) keeps plain `pr` products. Its pair level is
a fabric register `prq[q] <= pr[2q] + pr[2q+1]` (17-bit signed) feeding the same `s3` form.
`g_casc` (IMPL=1) is untouched.

Why the results are bit-identical: `s4[j]` is still the exact integer sum_i a_j[i]*w[i]. Every
intermediate value is exact and fits its width: |pm| <= 2^30, |pq| < 2^32 in 34 bits, s3 in
20 bits, s4 in 32 bits. Integer addition is associative, so regrouping (pairs, then 8, then D/16)
changes nothing. Everything after s4 (i2f, fp multiplies, isum_4, drain) is untouched.

## Expected
- DSP: 142, unchanged (the same 128 DSPs, now also using ALU and PREG).
- FF: about -1200. The 1280 `s2` flops go into the DSP P registers; `s3` is 20 bits instead of 24.
- LUT: about -2000 to -3000. Per column, fabric reductions drop from 127 to 63. The 128 column-0
  borrow addends disappear. The remaining s3 level is an 8-operand compressor, as big as today's
  s4 or column-0 s2.
- Area-equivalent: about -10% (24168 to roughly 21500 to 22000).
- fmax: neutral or better. The first fabric level now starts at a PREG (329 ps clock-to-out)
  instead of MREG to P comb (1671 ps). The 8-operand s3 add is no deeper than today's column-0 s2
  or s4. The critical path (drain/RMAX cone, 4.73 ns) is elsewhere, so est fmax stays about
  124 MHz, well above the 110 MHz target.

## Risks
- Yosys may not pack `pm + PK` as the post-adder of DSP 2q (constant C, PREG=0). A fabric +PK
  adder on 64 pairs would cost about 1.5k to 2k LUTs and eat most of the gain. Check the stat
  (LUT count) and the DSP OPMODEs. Fallback without PK: `pq = pm[2q+1] + pm[2q]`, with
  g = (pq[15:0] == 16'h8000) (the only ambiguous low value, O = +32768), odd value =
  $signed({pq[15] & ~g, pq[15:0]}) and even value = $signed(pq[32:16]) + (pq[15] & ~g).
  That is about 3 LUTs per pair, still a large net gain.
- DSP packing is fragile. Keep `pm`/`pq` as packed vectors (lesson r20260924-030158-s0), keep the
  mul and add with no logic between them, and make sure `pm[2q]` feeds only the `+PK` add.
- If `xilinx_dsp_cascade` turns C into PCIN, real placement needs the pair in adjacent DSP sites,
  which is the normal cascade case. The out-of-context yosys numbers are unaffected.
- Widths and sign: the odd column's low field must be read unsigned (zero-extended) and corrected
  by -(D/2)*PK. Reading it signed or dropping the correction breaks bit-exactness, and the
  tests/test_rtl.py fuzz and MLP runs (negative activations/weights, -128 corners) would catch it.
implementation:
# DSP post-adder pair sums in `g_tree` (rtl/mxu/otpu_mxu.sv)

- `pp` (32-bit) is now `pm` (34-bit packed products, `34'(pa) * 34'($signed(w))`). A new packed register `pq[p][q] <= pm[p][2q+1] + (pm[p][2q] + PK)` with `PK = 34'd32513` holds the pair sums. That is meant to be the DSP post-adder plus PREG. `pm[2q]` feeds only the `+PK` add.
- The fabric `s2` level is gone. `s3[j][g]` (now 20-bit) sums 8 pair values. Even column: `$signed(pq[32:16])`. Odd column: `pq[15:0]` read zero-extended. The last column when MCOLS is odd: fabric `prq[q] = pr[2q] + pr[2q+1]` (17-bit).
- `s4[j]` starts at `-(D/2)*PK` for odd j (always a packed column) and at 0 otherwise. There are still 4 register levels, so `LDOT`, `m1..m4` and `ws1..ws4` are unchanged. `g_casc` is untouched.
- Checked: verilator lint of the RTL_SOURCES set is clean. Passing: `test_mlp_rtl[1]`, `test_fuzz_single_slice[0]`, `test_design_size_block_128_rtl`.
- Not checked: yosys packing (whether `+PK` lands in the post-adder of DSP 2q with PREG=0, and in the P register of DSP 2q+1). Check the LUT/FF stat. If `+PK` ends up in fabric, use the no-PK fallback in HYPOTHESIS.md. The odd-MCOLS path (`prq`) compiles, but no test config exercises it.
lesson: ACCEPTED (-13.1% area @123MHz): DSP48 post-adder (M+C, odd PK=32513 bias so fields extract exactly, no borrow) replaced first g_tree fabric level; use idle DSP P/ALU before adding LUT adders.

title: RMAX: keep the running max as ordered keys, and launch the ACC-path column hits from a flop

# RMAX: keep the running max as ordered keys, and launch the ACC-path column hits from a flop

Category: timing

## Motivation
The reported critical path (4.777 ns, 123 MHz) is the ACC-path RMAX update:

    SRL16E.CLK->Q (1.47 ns)            u_rw.g_regs.qr[8] = rw.col[1][0] (yosys turns the keep'd
                                        last stage into an SRL, see LESSONS r012715)
    LUT3 -> LUT5 -> LUT4 -> LUT4        column match, mx[j] mux, then ftz(mx[j]) (8-bit exponent==0
                                        detect) and fkey's sign-conditional invert, all AFTER the mux
    LUT6 -> CARRY4 x3                   fkey(ry[k]) > fkey(mx[j])
    LUT6 -> LUT2 -> LUT5 -> FDRE.CE     !mx_have || gt, OR over lanes/sources -> CE of mx[j]

About 1.5 ns is the SRL clock-to-out of `rw` and ~1.4 ns is the col-select + ftz/fkey on the
*stored* max, which is pure redundancy: `mx[j]` only ever holds `ftz(x)`, so `ftz(mx[j])` is the
identity, and fkey could be computed once when the value is written instead of on every compare.
Earlier rounds attacked single pieces of this cone (registering rz: +0.9%; constant-index compare:
+2.6%) and each time the rest of the same cone stayed critical (LESSONS r031957-s0, r034118-s0:
"the ftz/fkey + carry + CE fan-out is the cone"). This change removes all three pieces at once:
the SRL launch, the column decode, and the fkey/ftz on the stored side.

## Change (rtl/mxu/otpu_mxu.sv only)
1. **Store the running max as its sort key.** Replace `f32_t mx[MCOLS]` with
   `logic [31:0] mk[MCOLS]` holding `fkey(value)` (otpu_fp::fkey = ftz, then
   `s ? ~a : {1,a[30:0]}`). Update rule in both the rx and rw blocks:
   `if (!mx_have[j] || fkey(c) > mk[j]) mk[j] <= fkey(c);` with c = rx.nv[k] / ry[k].
   Write-out (mx_go) converts back: `unkey(k) = k[31] ? {1'b0, k[30:0]} : ~k`, i.e.
   `t_wdata[k] = unkey(mk[...])` (per bit an XOR with k[31], in the non-critical write mux).
   Bit-exactness: `fp_gt(c, mx) == (fkey(c) > fkey(mx))` by definition, and `fkey(mx) == mk`
   because mx is always stored ftz'd (`fkey(ftz(x)) == fkey(x)`). `unkey(fkey(ftz(x))) == ftz(x)`:
   for sign 0 the key is `{1, a[30:0]}` -> `{0, a[30:0]}`; for sign 1 the key is `~a` (bit 31 = 0)
   -> `~~a`. +0 and -0 keep distinct keys (0x80000000 / 0x7FFFFFFF), exactly as today. NaNs are not
   special-cased by fkey today either, so they map identically. The initial/reset value of mk is
   irrelevant (guarded by mx_have, as now).
   Now the stored side of the comparator is a bare flop (mux by column only), and fkey(candidate)
   is computed from flops (ry is the fadd's `r` register, rx.nv is a register) in parallel.
2. **Precompute the rw column hits one-hot and end them in a reset flop.** From r1 (flops) compute
   `rh[k][j] = r1.v && c_rmax && r1.m[k] && (r1.col[k][MW-2:0] == j)` for k < NL, j < MCOLS
   (4 bits here), delay it through `otpu_delay #(.N(LM + LA - 1))` with `en(t_gnt)`, and end in
   `always_ff if (rst) rwh <= '0; else if (t_gnt) rwh <= rh_p;` (a reset stage cannot become an
   SRL -- same trick as mt/ws6/asq). Total delay LM+LA, same enable as u_rw, so rwh is exactly the
   hits of rw. The rw RMAX block uses `rwh[k][j]` instead of `rw.v && c_rmax && rw.m[k]` + the col
   decode. u_rw itself is unchanged (it still carries v/m/ad for the TMEM write-back, which isn't
   critical). c_rmax is constant while entries are in flight (q_h flips only after c_drained,
   which waits for rmw_n == 0), so folding it in early is exact.
3. **Keep the compare out of the D mux.** Write the update per column:
   `hit_j = OR_k rwh[k][j]` (resp. rx hits), `cand_j` = the key of the lane that hits column j
   (selected by the hit bits only), `upd_j = OR_k hit[k][j] && (!mx_have[j] || key_k > mk[j])`,
   `if (upd_j) mk[j] <= cand_j`. Exact because at most one lane hits a given column per cycle
   (lanes drain distinct columns dj+k) and rx/rw updates are mutually exclusive (rx needs
   !c_acc, rw entries exist only for c_acc commands, and c_acc is fixed for the command whose
   entries are in flight); when both would be absent nothing changes. So the compare only drives
   the CE, and the D input is a hit-selected mux of precomputed keys.

Nothing else changes: same values, same cycles, same TMEM traffic, no added latency.

## Expected
- Critical cone becomes: FF clk-Q (~0.4) -> exponent-zero/fkey of the candidate (2 LUT) -> compare
  LUT6 -> 3x CARRY4 -> 2 LUTs -> CE, roughly 3.0-3.3 ns (was 4.78). The rx path gets the same
  benefit. The next cone in the histogram sits at ~4.06-4.30 ns (the big 3.82-4.06 bucket is the
  fp pipelines), so logic delay should land around 4.1-4.3 ns: est fmax ~130-138 MHz (+6-12%).
- Area: removes the ftz+fkey logic on the stored side of each comparator (~30-40 LUTs per lane per
  source) and the rw col decode; adds a 4-bit x 6 hit delay line (a few SRL LUTs + 4 FFs) and the
  32-bit unkey on the write-out (~32 LUTs, merges into the existing t_wdata mux). Net ~ -20 to
  +20 LUT, +4-8 FF: area within +-0.2%. Acceptance through the fmax >= +3% rule.

## Risks
- If the 4.3-4.54 ns bucket (~260 endpoints) belongs to another cone (e.g. drain lane selection /
  bank-conflict chain into r0 or rf_h), the gain caps at the step to that cone (still >= +5% if it
  is below ~4.5 ns).
- Getting the key/unkey mapping wrong on sign/zero would change RMAX outputs (-0 vs +0, subnormals
  flushed): covered by the RMAX tests; the derivation above is exact for every 32-bit pattern.
- The hit delay line must use exactly LM+LA stages with en = t_gnt, or RMAX would compare against
  the wrong lane's column; and the exclusivity argument (one lane per column, rx vs rw) must hold --
  if in doubt keep the original priority (rw over rx, later lane over earlier) in the D mux, at the
  cost of the compare feeding D as well as CE.
- Verilator lint: `mk` / hit arrays are new names only; no port changes.
implementation:
# RMAX: running max as ordered keys, rw column hits from a flop (rtl/mxu/otpu_mxu.sv)

- `f32_t mx[MCOLS]` is now `logic [31:0] mk[MCOLS]` holding `fkey(max)`. The write-out (mx_go) uses a local `unkey(k) = k[31] ? {0,k[30:0]} : ~k`, and `unkey(fkey(ftz(x))) == ftz(x)` holds for every bit pattern, so the TMEM values are unchanged.
- The rw hits are precomputed one-hot from r1: `rh[k][j] = r1.v && c_rmax && r1.m[k] && col==j`. They go through `otpu_delay #(N=LM+LA-1, en=t_gnt)` and end in a reset flop `rwh`, for LM+LA stages total with the same enable as u_rw. u_rw is unchanged and still drives the TMEM write-back. The rx hits (`rxh`) are decoded combinationally from the rx register.
- A per-column always_comb builds `mx_hit` (OR of hits), `mx_cand` (hit-selected AND-OR of the candidate keys `fkey(rx.nv[k])` / `fkey(ry[k])`) and `mx_upd` (`hit && (!mx_have || key > mk[j])`). In the t_gnt branch: `if (mx_upd[j]) mk[j] <= mx_cand[j]; if (mx_hit[j]) mx_have[j] <= 1`. The compare only drives the CE.
- The AND-OR mux depends on "at most one hit per column per cycle": lanes drain distinct columns, and rx (only !c_acc) and rw (only c_acc) never overlap because q_h flips only once drained. I added an `ifndef SYNTHESIS` `$fatal` that checks this every granted cycle.
- Checks: the lint is clean. These passed: test_mlp_rtl[1], test_fuzz_single_slice, test_scoreboard_stress_single_slice, test_lane_count_does_not_change_results and test_attention_layer_rtl (25 tests). No other files were edited.
lesson: RMAX stored as fkey + flopped one-hot rw column hits (removes SRL launch, col decode, stored-side ftz/fkey): only +1.4% fmax, -0.4% area. The fkey(candidate) compare, carry chain and CE fan-out still set the limit.

title: Size the dot-product result (s4) and its int->fp32 conversion to the exact SW = 16 + clog2(D) bits, with an i2f that has no rounding step
hypothesis:
# Size the dot-product result (s4) and its int->fp32 conversion to the exact SW = 16 + clog2(D) bits, with an i2f that has no rounding step

Category: area

## Motivation
The champion computes every column's exact integer dot product `s4` at **32 bits**. The odd
column's accumulator starts at `-32'(D/2*PK)` and every `s3` term is sign-extended to 32 bits.
Yosys can't tell that the sum never overflows 23 bits, so it keeps the full width in these places:

- the s4 adder chain: 2 columns x 8 adds (7 s3 terms plus the PK bias on the odd column) x 32 bits,
  plus the 32-bit s4 register;
- `i2f_s1`: a 32-bit negate, zero detect and `lzc32`, and a 32+6+2-bit `im` register;
- `i2f_s2`: a 32-bit barrel shift, then a round step that can never fire: the guard/sticky OR,
  the 25-bit `mr` incrementer, the `mr[24]` renormalize mux and `e + 1`.

The dot product of D int8 x int8 products lies in [-D*16256, D*16384]. So |s4| <= D*2^14 < 2^(15+clog2 D).
For the board's D=128 it fits a **23-bit signed** value with a 22-bit magnitude. A magnitude of at
most 24 bits converts to fp32 exactly, so i2f's rounding logic is dead hardware.

History supports this. r20260924-030158-s1 narrowed the tree plus s4 and added a round-free i2f.
That was bit-exact and cut area by 2.2%, but it was not accepted only because fmax was 109 MHz,
under the 110 MHz target. The champion now runs at 123 MHz, so the fmax gate is no longer a
problem. The later post-adder change (r20260924-034118-s1) replaced the first tree levels but kept
s4 and i2f at 32 bits. That part of the saving is still available. Per LESSONS: "yosys can't
narrow widths itself, so size them in the RTL".

## Change (rtl/mxu/otpu_mxu.sv only)
1. Add these localparams:
   ```systemverilog
   localparam int SW = 16 + $clog2(D);   // exact signed width of a dot product: |dot| <= D*2^14
   localparam int MG = SW - 1;           // magnitude bits (|dot| < 2^MG)
   localparam int LZW = $clog2(MG);
   ```
   Declare `logic signed [SW-1:0] s4 [MCOLS]`, which was `[31:0]`.
2. In `g_tree`, compute the s4 sum in SW bits:
   `t = (j % 2 == 1) ? SW'(-(D/2*int'(PK))) : '0; t = t + SW'(s3[j][g]) ...`.
   Two's-complement wraparound in SW bits is exact because the final value fits in SW bits
   (the intermediate bias + partial sums can wrap harmlessly). s3 stays 20 bits.
   In `g_casc` (IMPL=1, not synthesized here), assign `s4[j] = SW'(t)`. The value is the same
   exact integer, so the truncation is lossless.
3. Replace `i2f_mid_t im[MCOLS]` and `i2f_s1`/`i2f_s2` with local, narrowed versions. Stages and
   latency stay the same (S5 = negate + LZC, S6 = shift + pack), so m5/m6/ws5/ws6 alignment is
   unchanged:
   ```systemverilog
   typedef struct packed { logic z, s; logic [LZW-1:0] lz; logic [MG-1:0] mag; } dmid_t;
   function automatic dmid_t d2f_s1(input logic signed [SW-1:0] x);
     dmid_t m;
     m.z   = (x == 0);
     m.s   = x[SW-1];
     m.mag = MG'(x[SW-1] ? -x : x);                      // |x| < 2^MG
     m.lz  = LZW'(lzc32(32'(m.mag) << (32 - MG)));        // leading zeros within MG bits
     return m;
   endfunction
   function automatic f32_t d2f_s2(input dmid_t m);
     logic [MG-1:0] nrm;
     if (m.z) return F_ZERO;
     nrm = m.mag << m.lz;                                 // nrm[MG-1] = 1
     return {m.s, 8'(126 + MG - int'(m.lz)), 23'(nrm[MG-2:0]) << (24 - MG)};
   endfunction
   ```
   Generate-guard it with `if (MG <= 24)`. Otherwise keep the old `i2f_s1(32'(s4[j]))` /
   `i2f_s2` path. No shipping configuration takes the fallback (D <= 512).

**Why it is bit-identical to `i2f(32'(s4))`:**
- For nonzero x with a magnitude below 2^24, `lzc32` of the 32-bit magnitude is lzm + (32 - MG),
  so `e = 158 - lz = 126 + MG - lzm`.
- `nrm32 = mag << lz` has its leading one at bit 31, and `nrm32[7:0] == 0` because lz >= 8.
  So g = st = 0, `mr = mm`, and `mr[24] = 0`: no rounding and no renormalization.
- The fraction `nrm32[30:8]` is `{nrm[MG-2:0], (24-MG) zeros}`, which is exactly the expression
  above. The sign is x's sign bit, and x == 0 gives F_ZERO in both versions.
- The ws/ascale multiplies, partial loop and combine are unchanged, so every fp32 rounding and
  the operation order stay the same.

## Expected
Estimated at D=128, MCOLS=2:
- **LUT:** about -400 to -450. The s4 chains lose 9 bits x 8 adds x 2 columns (~140). Per column,
  negate/LZC loses ~20 and the shifter ~40. The round path (25-bit incrementer, sticky, 23-bit
  renormalize mux, e+1) loses ~70 per column.
- **FF:** about -40 (s4: 2 x 9; im: 2 x 11).
- **DSP, BRAM:** unchanged.
- **Area-equivalent:** about -420 to -470, which is -2.0% to -2.3% against 21008. That clears the
  -1% acceptance bar.
- **fmax:** unchanged or slightly better, around 123 MHz. The critical path runs from the drain RMW
  to the RMAX flop CE (SRL `u_rw` -> fkey compare -> CE), not through the dot product or i2f.
  Shorter s4 carry chains and a smaller i2f can only help the S4/S5/S6 cones.

## Risks
- **Range argument:** the change relies on each operand being a genuine int8 (w0 and a0 bytes are
  8-bit), so |dot| <= D*2^14. D is a multiple of 16, and for D that is not a power of two
  `clog2` rounds up, which only adds margin.
- **Odd-column PK bias:** `D/2*PK` exceeds SW bits for larger D, but only the final wrapped sum
  matters, and that sum is exact modulo 2^SW. For D=128 the bias (-2080832) fits in 23 bits anyway.
- **Lint:** Verilator width warnings are non-fatal (`-Wno-WIDTH*`), but use explicit `SW'()` and
  `MG'()` casts to keep them quiet.
- **Casts and edge widths:**
  - The `-x` in `d2f_s1` is SW bits wide. Truncating to MG bits is safe because the most negative
    SW value (-2^(SW-1)) can't occur.
  - If D=16 (SW=20, MG=19), the `<< (24 - MG)` shift is 5. That is fine.
  - If MG = 24, the shift is 0. That is also fine.

# Drain control off the carry chains: MW-bit drain column counters + RMAX kept as ordered keys

Category: timing

## Motivation
The two slowest cones in the MXU both sit in the drain stage, and their delays are within 1.5% of
each other. That is why the last three single-cone attempts ended as no_gain:

1. **RMAX update (champion critical path, 4.777 ns):** SRL clk->Q of `u_rw` (rw.col) -> column
   decode -> `mx[j]` mux -> ftz/fkey of the stored max -> `fp_gt` CARRY4 x3 -> LUT6/LUT2/LUT5 ->
   `mx[j]` CE.
2. **Drain lane selection (4.705 ns).** This path appeared once r20260924-035327-s0 removed cone 1.
   That run's `build/tourney/otpu_mxu/r20260924-035327-s0/otpu_mxu/sta.txt` shows it:
   `dj` FDRE -> INV -> CARRY4 (`dj + k`) -> LUT6 -> CARRY4 (`< c_M`) -> LUT2 x3 (used/stop/ncnt) ->
   CARRY4 x2 (`dj + ncnt == c_M`, 8 bit) -> LUT4 -> LUT5 -> LUT3 -> LUT2 -> LUT3 -> CE
   (drain_row_done fanning out to dad/rf_h/dj/rf_n/rows_live). That run's gain was capped at
   +1.4% (4.777 -> 4.705 ns).

Earlier single fixes of cone 1 gave +0.9%, +2.6% and +1.4%, and the next cone was always right
behind. +3% needs logic <= ~4.64 ns, so both cones have to go in the same change.
The drain cone is pure arithmetic width. `dj` is 8 bits and the lane test is a 32-bit
`32'(dj)+32'(k) < 32'(c_M)`, but `dj` only ranges over 0..MCOLS-1 (M <= MCOLS; isasim.py:187
rejects anything else). With MCOLS=2 each of the three carry chains collapses to a 2- or 3-bit
function that fits in one LUT.

## Change (rtl/mxu/otpu_mxu.sv only)
**A. Drain column bookkeeping in MW bits** (MW = clog2(MCOLS)+1 already holds 0..MCOLS):
- `logic [MW-1:0] dj; logic [MW-1:0] ncnt;` (were 8 bits). Add `wire [MW-1:0] c_Mn = MW'(c_M);`.
  This is exact because 0 < M <= MCOLS < 2^MW, which the ISA requires (isasim `0 < M <= cfg.MCOLS`;
  the result FIFO and dval_l indexing `MW'(dj+k)` already assume it).
- In the drain always_comb, the lane test becomes
  `(MW+1)'(dj) + (MW+1)'(k) < (MW+1)'(c_Mn)`. No overflow: dj+k <= 2*MCOLS-2 < 2^(MW+1).
  Index `dad[]` and `rf_v[rf_h][]` with `MW'(dj) + MW'(k)` (the same index as today for every
  reachable value). `dcol_l[k] = 8'(dj) + 8'(k)` keeps the column field type unchanged.
  `ncnt = ncnt + 1'b1` stays the same (ncnt <= NL <= MCOLS fits).
- `drain_row_done = drain_go && (dj + ncnt == c_Mn)` in MW bits: no overflow, since dj + ncnt <= M.
  The advance is `dj <= dj + ncnt` in MW bits, and every reset or clear of `dj` stays `'0`.
- `32'(k) < 32'(ncnt)` in the t_* and r0/rx mask loops is unchanged (it widens a smaller value).
The drain issues the same lanes, addresses, values, columns and row-done cycles for every legal
command. Only the widths of values that never exceed MCOLS change.

**B. RMAX stored as sort keys with flopped one-hot rw column hits.** This is the same code as
`tools/tourney/runs/otpu_mxu/patches/r20260924-035327-s0.patch`, which already passed lint, the
fast set, the board set and perf bit-exactly. Apply it unchanged:
- `mx[MCOLS]` becomes `mk[MCOLS] = fkey(max)`. Write-out goes through
  `unkey(k) = k[31] ? {0,k[30:0]} : ~k`, and `unkey(fkey(ftz(x))) == ftz(x)` holds for every bit
  pattern. `fp_gt(c, mx) == fkey(c) > fkey(mx)` and `fkey(mx) == mk` because mx is always
  stored ftz'd.
- The rw hits `rh[k][j] = r1.v && c_rmax && r1.m[k] && col==j` go through
  `otpu_delay #(N=LM+LA-1, en=t_gnt)` and end in a reset flop `rwh`: LM+LA stages in total, with
  the same enable as u_rw. The rx hits are decoded from the rx register.
- Per column, the candidate key is AND-OR selected by the hits, and the compare only drives the CE
  (`mx_upd`). There is at most one hit per column per cycle: lanes drain distinct columns, and
  rx (!c_acc) and rw (c_acc) are exclusive because q_h flips only once drained. Keep the
  `ifndef SYNTHESIS` $fatal check.

The values, cycles, TMEM traffic and handshakes stay the same, and no latency is added.

## Expected
- Cone 2 goes from about 4.7 ns to about 2.5 ns: dj FF -> dad index mux / 3-bit bank compare
  (1-2 LUTs) -> ncnt -> 2-bit `== c_Mn` -> AND with rf_n/t_gnt -> CE. That also removes most
  of the (4.30, 4.54] bucket (~250 endpoints). They look like the same drain logic: r0/rx data and
  masks, dad/daddr muxes and the t_* outputs, all gated by ncnt/stop.
- Cone 1 was already below 4.705 ns in 035327-s0 (estimated ~3.3 ns).
- The next limiter should be the i2f d2f_s1 (23-bit negate + LZC, ~4.3-4.4 ns) or the fp pipeline
  bucket (<= 4.06 ns). Logic should land at ~4.3-4.5 ns, for an est fmax of ~130-136 MHz
  (+6 to +10%, with +3% needed).
- Area: fewer carry chains and compare LUTs in the drain (~-40 to -80 LUT), plus the RMAX -0.4%
  measured in 035327-s0. Net area ~-0.5 to -1%, FF about +4 (rwh) - 6 (dj/ncnt bits).
  Acceptance comes through the fmax >= +3% rule with area <= +1%.

## Risks
- If the (4.30, 4.54] bucket is a third cone (e.g. d2f_s1 at ~4.5 ns), the gain is capped around
  +5-6%. That is still above +3% unless it sits at >= 4.64 ns. If so, a follow-up could split
  d2f_s1 (negate | LZC).
- Narrowing relies on M <= MCOLS. An illegal M > MCOLS would drain differently, but it is already
  unsupported: rf_v and dval_l index with `MW'(dj+k)`, and the ISA simulator rejects it.
- Part B's exclusivity and hit-delay-length arguments are unchanged from 035327-s0, which passed
  every gate. Merge conflicts are unlikely: the patch touches only the RMAX block, and the
  champion since then changed only s4/i2f.
- Verilator lint: the width casts in the lane test and `dj + ncnt` must be explicit (MW-bit
  operands) to avoid WIDTH warnings.

The lane test is `(MW+1)'(dj) + (MW+1)'(k) < (MW+1)'(c_Mn)`. `dad`/`rf_v` are indexed with `MW'(dj) + MW'(k)`, `dcol_l[k] = 8'(dj) + 8'(k)`, and `drain_row_done` compares `MW'(dj + ncnt) == c_Mn`. title: Trim the drain's unreachable TMEM lanes (ASCALE load, RMAX write-out, drain) to NL and drop the dead bits carried by the u_rw delay line

# Trim the drain's unreachable TMEM lanes (ASCALE load, RMAX write-out, drain) to NL and drop the dead bits carried by the u_rw delay line

Category: area

## Motivation
With the board parameters (MCOLS = 2, LANES = 8, NL = min(LANES, MCOLS) = 2), three blocks of
the TMEM port logic in `otpu_mxu.sv` still loop over all LANES = 8 lanes. The ISA guarantees
`0 < M <= MCOLS`: `isasim.py:187` rejects anything else, and the RTL already depends on it
because `dad`, `q_jo`, `rf_v` and `mx` have only MCOLS entries. So lanes k >= 2 can never be
enabled, but Yosys can't prove that because `c_M`, `al_i` and `mx_i` are registers:

- **ASCALE load (`al_go`)**: for each of 8 lanes, a 32-bit `c_asa + al_i + k` address adder,
  a 32-bit `al_i + k < c_M` compare and the `t_raddr` / `t_ren` merge.
- **RMAX write-out (`mx_go`)**: for each of 8 lanes, a 32-bit `q_mxo + mx_i + k` adder, a
  compare and a 32-bit data mux `mx[MW'(mx_i + k)]`. Even lanes 0 and 1 get a variable-index
  mux here, because `mx_i` is a register.
- **Drain (`drain_go`)**: for each of 8 lanes, a `k < ncnt` compare and the `t_raddr` /
  `t_waddr` / `t_wdata` merge. `ncnt` is at most NL = 2, but Yosys can't bound it.
- **`al_i` / `mx_i`**: two 8-bit step counters with their adders. With MCOLS <= LANES the
  first step always finishes, so both stay at 0 forever.

Rough size of the dead logic: about 12 extra 32-bit adders, 6 to 8 32-bit muxes and 16
compares, so roughly 600 to 800 LUTs out of 10207.

This isn't a guess from reading the code. Round r20260924-033026-s1 proposed the same trim and
measured **-2.9% area at 122 MHz** (outcome `improvement`). It lost that round to s0's fmax win
(orchestrator.py:287 merges only the top gain per round), and its worktree was dropped. The
current source still has the `LANES` loops. The champion has shrunk since then (-13.1% and
-1.5%), so the same absolute saving is now a larger share, about 3 to 3.5%.

A second, smaller item in the same drain logic: the `u_rw` delay line (`otpu_delay`, N = LM + LA =
6) carries the whole `rmw_t` struct `r1`. Its last stage `qr` is `(* keep *)`, so bits that
nothing reads are kept anyway, along with the SRL stages that feed them:
- `rw.nv` (NL x 32 = 64 bits): nothing reads it. The write data is `ry`, from the fmadd.
- `rw.col[k][7:1]` (NL x 7 = 14 bits): only `col[MW-2:0]` (1 bit) is ever read.

That is 78 SRL16 plus 78 FDRE held alive only by `keep`. The same 7 dead col bits per lane
also sit in `r0`, `r1` and `rx`.

## Change (only rtl/mxu/otpu_mxu.sv)
1. Add `localparam bit AL1 = (MCOLS <= LANES);` (the ASCALE load and RMAX write-out each take
   one step) and `localparam int CW = (MCOLS > 1) ? $clog2(MCOLS) : 1;` (column index width).
   Add `wire [7:0] al_o = AL1 ? 8'd0 : al_i;` and `wire [7:0] mx_o = AL1 ? 8'd0 : mx_i;`, and
   use `al_o` / `mx_o` wherever `al_i` / `mx_i` is read as an offset.
2. In the TMEM `always_comb`, change the loop bounds of the `drain_go`, `al_go` and `mx_go`
   blocks from `k < LANES` to `k < NL`. When MCOLS > LANES, NL = LANES, so that case is
   unchanged. With AL1, the RMAX write data becomes `mx[k]` (a constant index, no mux) and the
   addresses become `c_asa + k` / `q_mxo + k`.
3. In the sequential block:
   - `mx_done`: set it when `AL1 || mx_o + LANES >= c_M`.
   - `al_st`: go to 2 when `AL1 || al_o + LANES >= c_M`.
   - ASCALE load: `for (k < NL) if (al_o + k < MCOLS) alpha[MW'(al_o + k)] <= t_rdata[k]`.
     For MCOLS <= LANES this is `alpha[k] <= t_rdata[k]`, as before.
   - `al_i` / `mx_i` stay in the code, but with AL1 nothing reads them, so Yosys removes them.
4. Narrow `rmw_t.col` to `logic [NL-1:0][CW-1:0]` and assign `r0.col` / `rx.col` from
   `dcol_l[k][CW-1:0]`. Replace the reads `rx.col[k][MW-2:0]`, `rw.col[k][MW-2:0]` and
   `r0.col[k][MW-2:0]` with `.col[k]`. (MW - 1 = $clog2(MCOLS) = CW, so the same bits are read.)
5. Make `u_rw` carry only the fields read after the fmadd. Define
   `typedef struct packed { logic v; logic [NL-1:0] m; logic [NL-1:0][31:0] ad; logic [NL-1:0][CW-1:0] col; } rwd_t;`,
   declare `rwd_t rw`, and feed `u_rw` from `'{v: r1.v, m: r1.m, ad: r1.ad, col: r1.col}`.
   The fmadd still reads `r1.nv` directly. The `rw.v`, `rw.m`, `rw.ad` and `rw.col` users keep
   the same field names.

### Why the results stay bit-identical
Assume `0 < M <= MCOLS <= LANES`; the ISS enforces the first bound.
- **Lanes k >= NL**: under the old code, `k < ncnt` and `al_i + k < c_M` and `mx_i + k < c_M`
  were all false for these lanes (al_i = mx_i = 0, k >= MCOLS >= M). So `t_ren`, `t_wen`,
  `t_raddr`, `t_waddr` and `t_wdata` for those lanes were already constant 0. They still are.
- **al_i / mx_i**: the first `al_go` / `mx_go` step already met `0 + LANES >= c_M`, so they never
  left 0, and `mx_done` / `al_st = 2` were set on that same step. The cycle-by-cycle behavior of
  the ports, the grants and `done` is unchanged.
- **Dropped bits**: `rw.nv` and `col[k][7:CW]` had no readers, and the bits that are read are
  the same bits as before.
- **MCOLS > LANES**: AL1 = 0 and NL = LANES, so the code is the same as today.

The fp datapath, order of operations and rounding are untouched.

## Expected
- **LUT**: -550 to -800 (dead lane adders, compares and merges, the `mx` variable-index muxes,
  the `al_i` / `mx_i` counters).
- **LUT-RAM**: about -78 (u_rw SRLs for nv and the col upper bits).
- **FF**: about -130 (u_rw kept `qr` bits, col bits in r0/r1/rx, al_i/mx_i).
- **DSP / BRAM**: unchanged.
- **Area-equivalent**: about -700 to -950 of 20696, so **-3.5% to -4.5%**.
- **fmax**: neutral to slightly better (~123 MHz), well above the 110 MHz target. The
  critical path (u_rw SRL -> `fp_gt(ry, mx)` -> mx CE) reads a 1-bit col now instead of 8, and
  the `mx` write-out muxes are gone.
- **Performance**: cycle-identical, so no change in the Qwen3 proxy.

## Risks
- If a test issues M > MCOLS or M = 0, AL1 skips the multi-step path. The ISS rejects those
  commands (`0 < M <= MCOLS`), and the RTL already can't handle M > MCOLS (dad, rf_v and mx are
  sized MCOLS), so no valid test can reach this.
- CW for MCOLS = 1: the current `[MW-2:0]` slices are already zero-width there. Using
  CW = max(1, clog2) makes that case cleaner, not worse. Verilator lint must stay clean: watch
  for width warnings on `dcol_l[k][CW-1:0]` and the `'{...}` struct literal. If the literal
  triggers lint, use explicit field assignments into an `rwd_t` wire.
- Yosys may already have removed part of the lane logic through constant propagation, so the
  gain could come in below the earlier measurement. The fallback floor is the ~0.6% from item 5,
  plus whatever lane logic ABC didn't already strip.

  `al_o` / `mx_o` (0 when AL1, else `al_i` / `mx_i`), which now supply every ASCALE-load and RMAX-write-out offset.

- `u_rw` now carries a new `rwd_t {v, m, ad, col}` (no `nv`). The fmadd still reads `r1.nv`.

  built field by field in an `always_comb` into `rw1` (the fallback the hypothesis suggested).
- Checks: Verilator lint (given flags, otpu_top) is clean. Passing: `test_mlp_rtl[1]`, `test_fuzz_single_slice[0,1]`,
